title: Warming delays photosynthesis downregulation but not growth in a boreal conifer
content: Plants in higher latitudes adjust their activity (e.g. photosynthesis and tissue development) in response to intra-annual changes in environmental conditions, such as the number of light hours (i.e. photoperiod), radiation intensity, temperature, or water availability. This intra-annual variability leads to physiological activity that is highly reduced in winter, when temperatures, photoperiod, and incoming radiation are low, and peaks around the summer solstice, when radiation levels are optimal and temperatures and water availability have not yet become limiting. While these phenological adjustments in plant function are obvious in deciduous species, evergreen species also modulate their physiological activity in response to intra-annual environmental variability.
